Commentary.Commentary: That's it from us then! It was another close game and hope you enjoyed the coverage. Do join us on 31st August for the 4th ODI which will be played at the same venue and at the same time, 1430 IST. Until then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

TILLAKARATNE DILSHAN says he made the right decision to retire here. He is really happy with the way he has finished his career. Adds when he woke up in the morning he decided to give up on his One Day career as well. He feels this is the time to give the youngsters a chance. Adds that he feels he has done enough for his country and now the youngsters can take Sri Lankan cricket forward. Says he wanted to do some or the other thing for his side like if he failed with the bat then he wanted to contribute with the ball. Adds even today he feels he is a youngster and he is really happy now. Feels there are lots of ups and downs in one's career so thanks his wife for giving him a lot of courage and his parents and his fans for the support throughout. Says he has achieved a lot of things in cricket and thanks his wife and parents. He feels it was during the 2008 tour when he was dropped and that time he told Jayawardena to not to pick him in the middle order as he wanted to open the innings. He kept on scoring runs after that and he was happy with that as he had handy scores under his belt. Feels from 2009 to 2016 he scored more than 9000 runs. Says every decision he took has been going the right way for him. (On his Dilscoop) Says he practiced a lot in Sri Lanka. Says he did it first against Shane Watson in the 2009 World Cup in England where he got Man of the Tournament and after that he's happy that he has one shot under his name.

Australian captain, DAVID WARNER says it's always good to get a win and it's nice to be 2-1 up in the series. He feels the bowlers bowled well after the first 10 overs and credits Zampa and Hastings for bowling so well. Adds they wanted big partnerships with the bat.

Sri Lankan captain, ANGELO MATHEWS feels they were 20-30 runs short and it was disappointing to end up losing in spite of having these many spinners. Feels they lost some wickets in the middle and they could have done better. Adds the shot selection was pretty poor but credits the bowlers for bowling their hearts out. Says the wicket was really good and it was turning towards the end. He is gutted as they couldn't give Dilshan a fitting farewell and thanks the veteran for his services to Sri Lankan cricket.

Man of the Match, GEORGE BAILEY says they lost early wickets and the wicket was a nice one. Adds they did a lot of hard work and says it would have been nice if he had finished not out. Says you have to try something different so he played those sweep shots.

That also brings an end to Tillakaratne Dilshan's ODI career! He is being carried by his teammates. What a servant he has been for Sri Lanka. He amassed 10290 runs with 22 centuries. He's the only captain to score a ton in all three formats and holds the record for scoring most ODI runs after turning 35. What a remarkable career!

The Sri Lankan bowlers tried their best but the Australian batsmen batted really well. Mathews, Aponso and Dilruwan Perera finished with two wickets each while Prasanna and de Silva got one to their names each. Had there been 30-40 more runs, the result could have been different. Earlier, Sri Lanka won the toss and posted a total of 226 runs. Riding on Chandimal's spectacular century, the hosts posted a competitive total on the board.

Matthew Wade and George Bailey then added 81 runs for the 5th wicket which happened to be the best partnership of the match. That stand took Australia towards the 200-run mark. Once Wade was dismissed, Australia lost the momentum yet again. Bailey also got out but not after hitting a superb fifty. Faulkner failed to finish things as the Lankan spinners got some free wickets as Australia went for the glory shots. Eventually the visitors got past the line and chased down the total successfully.

Australia didn't get off to a good start as they lost Warner early once again. Mathews got the wicket of his counterpart and later on Finch was dismissed but replays showed he was not out. Shaun Marsh couldn't do much and Australia were in big trouble. George Bailey and Travis Head stitched a 62-run stand to rebuild things. Dilruwan Perera broke that partnership and the Aussies were in trouble again.

Phew! What a match! Australia had things under control at one stage but they stuttered towards the end. Sri Lanka gave their all but it wasn't enough to stop the Australians from taking a series lead of 2-1! Brilliant performance from the visitors though to chase down a tricky total.
